title: Infinitesimal neighbourhoods and associated graded rings under formally etale maps
statement:
Let $\varphi:A\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $J\subset C$ an ideal, and suppose the composite $A\to C/J$ is surjective with kernel $I$. Assume $\varphi$ is formally etale: for every $A$-algebra $E$ and square-zero ideal $N\subset E$, reduction induces a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{A\text{-alg}}(C,E)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{A\text{-alg}}(C,E/N)$. In particular this hypothesis holds if $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For every integer $n\ge1$, the map induced by $\varphi$ is an isomorphism
$$A/I^n\xrightarrow{\sim}C/J^n.$$
Consequently the canonical map
$$\operatorname{gr}_I(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{gr}_J(C)$$
is an isomorphism of graded $A/I=C/J$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. These are the maps $[a]\mapsto[\varphi(a)]$; hence they commute with compatible ring homomorphisms preserving the specified ideals, and with composition. No Noetherian, finite-generation or equality $J=IC$ assumption is imposed. Quotient rings, algebras and their homomorphisms are [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]; spectra are [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), including its inductive lifting proof; etale implies formally etale: Tag 00UR (lemma-formally-etale-etale). Naturality is that of the canonical quotient maps.

proof.text: For the parenthetical etale case, suppose $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale. By [def-weil-etale-morphism] it is flat and unramified, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-unramified-formally-etale] makes it formally smooth in the sense of [def-sbc-formally-smooth]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-affine-formally-smooth-iff-ring-lifting] to $\varphi$: for every $A$-algebra $E$ and square-zero ideal $N\subset E$, every $A$-algebra map $C\to E/N$ lifts to an $A$-algebra map $C\to E$, i.e. the reduction map of the item is surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], $\Omega_{C/A}=0$; the implication (2)$\Rightarrow$(1) of [lem-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-ring-iff-kahler-zero], with base ring $A$ and algebra $C$, says that such a lift is unique, i.e. the reduction map is injective. Hence the stated lifting hypothesis holds. In the rest of the proof use that lifting hypothesis directly; no finite-presentation assumption is needed there.

source.place: Tag 00UR (lemma-formally-etale-etale), etale implies formally etale, here via formally smooth plus formally unramified as in the cited nodes.

proof.text: Write $\pi_{I,n}:A\to A/I^n$ and $\pi_{J,n}:C\to C/J^n$ for the quotient maps [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. If $a\in I$ then $\varphi(a)\in J$, so a product of $n$ elements of $I$ maps into $J^n$; sums and multiples give $\varphi(I^n)\subseteq J^n$. Thus $f_n([a])=[\varphi(a)]$ is a well-defined $A$-algebra homomorphism. These maps commute with every reduction map, since both composites send $[a]$ to $[\varphi(a)]$. For $n=1$, $f_1$ is surjective by assumption, and $f_1([a])=0$ means $a\in I$, so it is injective. Set $g_1=f_1^{-1}$ and $\ell_1=g_1\pi_{J,1}$.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), proof: successive square-zero lifts and uniqueness; associated-graded conclusion in the statement, expanded on representatives.

proof.text: Induct on $n\ge1$ with claim that $f_n$ has an inverse $g_n$, compatible with every reduction to an earlier positive level. Step 2 is the base case. Given $g_n$, apply [lem-sfb-formally-etale-power-step] to the stated lifting hypothesis and the same $A,C,I,J$: it supplies the two-sided inverse $g_{n+1}$ and $r_ng_{n+1}=g_ns_n$. Composing this equality with earlier reductions preserves the inductive compatibility. Thus all the asserted quotient isomorphisms are obtained.

source.place: Tag 0H1D (lemma-formally-etale-lift-infinitesimal), proof: one successive dotted arrow, its factorization and the uniqueness argument for the inverse composite.

proof.text: Since $\varphi(I)\subseteq J$ and every $f_n=Q_n(\varphi)$ is an isomorphism, [lem-sfb-power-quotient-graded-comparison] applies and gives the stated graded $A/I=C/J$-algebra isomorphism, with precisely the homogeneous representative maps $[a]_r\mapsto[\varphi(a)]_r$, including degree zero. Its commuting-square, composition and identity formulas give all the required naturality assertions for both quotient and graded maps, even when the comparison maps are not formally etale. Neither cited argument requires $J=IC$ or finiteness hypotheses.
